what_happened: While working on a code request, Athena reached reading 1 and asked the reader a question that neither the repository nor the defaults answered. The question was what counts as success for the work. The reader answered that the outcome is the check behind the work: for the explainer, the audience rates the live page 4 or more. They added that an empty queue is not success, and that if the same item fails twice the loop should stop as thrashing. The event was logged as a correction, but it was an answered question.
cause: Requests name a deliverable, such as an explainer or a work loop, without saying how success is measured or when the loop should stop. Nothing in the system's defaults supplies a success measure or a stop rule for audience-facing quality or for loops. The reading step does not require Athena to settle these before the job starts, so the gap only shows up as a question to the user. A default that treated queue-drained as done would also have passed.
prevention: Add defaults that apply when a request has a quality outcome or a loop. (1) The outcome is the check behind the work, not the activity. Audience-facing quality is judged by a fresh model reader, with no part in building the work, who rates the live result as a newcomer. Below 4 of 5 blocks completion. (2) An empty queue or finished list is never success by itself. (3) If the same item fails twice, the loop stops and reports thrashing. The reading step should apply these defaults and record them as acceptance criteria, and ask the user only when the request contradicts them.
proposed_request: Add three standing defaults to Athena's reading step, so they apply whenever a request has a quality outcome or runs a loop over items. First, when the outcome is audience-facing quality (for example an explainer page), the reading must include an acceptance criterion that a fresh model reader, with no part in building the work, rates the live result as a newcomer, and that a rating below 4 of 5 blocks completion. Second, an empty queue or exhausted item list must never count as success on its own. The outcome check must also pass. Third, if the same item fails twice in a loop, the loop must stop and report thrashing instead of continuing. Apply these without asking the user, unless the request says otherwise. Show that a request for an explainer page gets these criteria in its reading with no question to the user.
